units.translation: The oar-blade of the linen-sewn ship, covering the sea, is its course.
I see a hawk rushing on wings in its course.
I am carried out of my course.
Falling from my course, I run,
Just as with horses I steer the chariot beyond the course,
There is nothing to learn outside the course,
Having been freed from the open-air frosts and dews.
He strikes me with a dark shower of bloody dew.
From the earth and from the sea dew.
With the dews of fierce lions.
He will banish him to desolate thickets or crags.
to cut through or to examine
Hesychius δρώπτειν: to cut through or to examine.
to cut through or to examine
Hesychius explains it as δυστυχία [misfortune], ἔνδεια [want], πόνος [toil], ταλαιπωρία [hardship]; Suidas as κακοπάθεια [suffering], δυστυχία [misfortune].
Of the torment of Prometheus fastened to the rock
Of the wanderings of Io over land and sea
Thus I corrected what is read in M with a metrical fault: πλευρὰς ὀδύνα [sides, pain]. Wieseler had already made it ὦ δύα [O misery].
You do not relent in bitter miseries.
Bent by countless calamities and miseries.
I escape unseemly bonds and miseries.
A stormy sea of ruinous misery indeed.
You hear of your father's dishonored miseries.
As recompense for the miseries of a mother's murder.
What misery again creeps into my sides?

Theognostus Can. p. 58, 9 notes this strange adjective, not knowing whence it was taken, among adjectives ending in ιος [ios], ἔχοντα ἐν τῇ πρώτη συλλαβῇ τὸ υ [having u in the first syllable]. In the passage of Aeschylus the reading is very uncertain, since only slight fragments of words remain from the preceding verses, so that we do not know whether δυΐαν [wretched] is correctly read or is corrupted from another word. Schwerdtius conjectured εἰδυῖα βόαμα φαίνω [knowing, I utter a cry], comparing the scholiast's note: οὐκέτι παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀκούσασα, ἀλλ᾽ αὐτόπτης γενομένη βοῶ [no longer having heard it from my father, but having become an eyewitness, I cry out].
having u in the first syllable
no longer having heard it from my father, but having become an eyewitness, I cry out
to be able, to have power
to be able, to have power

Thus Hermann emended what is in M: φωνεῖ · ὁ [he speaks; the] (sic, not ὁ [the]) δυνᾶσαι γάρ [for you are able]. The scholiast reads δύνασαι [you are able], who explains: ῥάδιον γὰρ τὸ εὔχεσθαι [for praying is easy].
You speak of greater things; for you are able.
I was not able to persuade the Titans.
For the revered Erinys has great power among the immortals.
For she is able, being closest to Zeus.
Not honoring the power of wealth, falsely stamped with praise.
Thus I emended for ὦ πολύκλαυτε φίλοισι θανών [O much-lamented, dead to your friends]. τί τάδε δυνάτα δυνάτα [why these mighty, mighty things] etc.
